transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24 10:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Nguyen (Redwood SE), Ava Brooks (Redwood CSM), Maria Lopez (AstraHealth CTO), Jared Kim (Lead ML), Priya Rao (SRE), Diego Martinez (PM)

Summary (auto): quick review of last week's benchmark numbers, discussed tuning knobs (batch size, KV cache, quantization), action items to run tail-latency focused tests, share security docs for private deploy.

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started in a sec. Can folks see the shared sheet? I posted the link in the calendar chat.
[00:12] Maria Lopez: Yep, I can see it. Thanks Samir. Trying to keep this short today, we've got exec sync at 11 so heads up.
[00:20] Jules Nguyen: Cool, quick agenda: results recap, tuning notes, open questions, next steps. We'll focus on latency/throughput vs what you have in production (BaselineAI).
[00:35] Jared Kim: Sounds good. we've been most worried about tail latency and cost. Also curious how much of the delta is quantization vs routing.
[00:48] Samir Patel: Right, perfect. Quick recap — the headline: across the representative 512-token prompt set, Redwood P50 was about 110ms vs BaselineAI 220ms, throughput on the same hardware config 120 requests/sec vs 85 rps. Those numbers are after enabling prefix KV cache and model quantization to int8-ish profile.
[01:15] Priya Rao: Wait, 110ms p50, that's impressive. What's the p95 look like? Our concern is spikes during peak.
[01:25] Jules Nguyen: Good Q. p95 for Redwood in these tests was around 450ms, baseline was 780ms. The tail improves if we tune batching and enable request prioritization; also caching really helps when you have repeated prefixes.
[01:45] Maria Lopez: Could you remind us what the baseline hardware was and whether you're comparing like-for-like GPUs?
[01:55] Samir Patel: Yes — baseline test used BaselineAI managed endpoints on A100-equivalent instances in the same cloud region. Our Redwood run used a similar instance class; where we differ is runtime optimizations — continuous batching, kernel selection, and the KV cache behavior. Also we ran a quantized variant which drops memory pressure and allows larger batch concurrency.
[02:20] Diego Martinez: When you say quantized, is that something you do server-side or do we need to re-export models? Our infra team is worried about accuracy regressions.
[02:31] Jules Nguyen: It's server-side. We onboard the quantized artifact to Redwood Dedicated or hosted; we have quality checks and evals against your prompt set to measure delta. For this POC we saw a <1% drop in relative task performance on the evals we ran.
[02:55] Maria Lopez: Hmm okay okay. Jared, did you look at the quality numbers?
[03:02] Jared Kim: I skimmed, looks acceptable but we want the detailed evaluation. Also, curious about throughput when sequence length varies — our production averages are closer to 800 tokens.
[03:15] Samir Patel: Great point. For 800-token runs our median shifts — Redwood P50 to ~160ms and Baseline to ~320ms. Throughput drops but the relative improvement stays roughly 1.8x. We'll include these additional sequences in the full spreadsheet.
[03:40] Priya Rao: Network jitter has been a thorn for us. If we move to Redwood Private (VPC), does that change the numbers significantly?
[03:50] Jules Nguyen: Private deployment actually reduces some of the network variability because you can keep traffic in your VPC and avoid public egress. In our experience, P50 might not move much but p95 can drop 10-20% depending on topology. We can run a staged test once we have your network diagram.
[04:15] Maria Lopez: Security questions: SOC2, KMS for keys, and audit logs — do you have a package we can hand to our compliance team?
[04:24] Ava Brooks: Yes, we have a security pack — SOC 2 reports, encryption-at-rest and in-transit details, KMS integrations and audit log examples. I'll share the packet after the call.
[04:38] Diego Martinez: Back to the numbers, can you explain how batch sizing impacted latency vs throughput in your runs?
[04:47] Jules Nguyen: Sure. We ran a sweep: batch size 1 to 16. At batch=1 latency lowest for P50 but throughput limited. At batch 8 is sweet spot for your prompt distribution: P50 went up ~30ms vs batch=1 but throughput scaled 3x. Our runtime supports dynamic batching with latency SLOs — we can cap per-route max batch or split small/large requests to different queues.
[05:20] Maria Lopez: So we could set a SLO to keep p95 under 600ms and you'd tune batching to meet it?
[05:27] Jules Nguyen: Exactly. We can enforce soft latency SLOs and prioritize small requests to keep spikes down.
[05:35] Jared Kim: I'm worried about cold-starts for KV cache when a new session begins. How many requests until the cache warms?
[05:44] Samir Patel: Typical warm-up for repeated prefixes is 2-4 requests for dominant prefixes. For diverse prompts it takes longer. We also support warm-up preloads if you can provide frequent prompts you expect.
[05:58] Priya Rao: Cost — how does the cost per 1M tokens compare with Baseline after quantization and batching?
[06:06] Samir Patel: Ballpark: after optimizations Redwood is about 20-30% lower on unit cost for your workload vs BaselineAI managed endpoints. Exact depends on reserved capacity and batching profiles. We'll model both hosted and dedicated options in the pricing spreadsheet.
[06:25] Diego Martinez: Did you include the additional engineering overhead for Private in that cost?
[06:29] Ava Brooks: We'll include a Private deployment add-on line — one-time setup and then a platform fee plus support. We can split TCO by 12/24/36 months in the doc.
[06:40] Maria Lopez: Any surprises in the logs? Errors, retry storms?
[06:44] Jules Nguyen: We saw a small number of retries in the baseline run correlated with preemption on their instances. Redwood Dedicated runs were stable; hosted had a couple of transient 503s in our earlier run but the tuned config eliminated them in the repeat.
[07:05] Jared Kim: Can you share the raw logs? We want to run our own analysis for p99 and tail correlations with sequence length.
[07:10] Samir Patel: Yep, we'll share logs and per-request latencies. That's in the action items.
[07:20] Diego Martinez: One more — how do fallbacks work if you lose capacity mid-rollout? We assume you have model variants.
[07:27] Jules Nguyen: We do. Smart routing can fallback to a smaller quantized variant or route to a different region or dedicated pool. We can configure auto-fallback thresholds.
[07:40] Maria Lopez: Good. Okay, sorry folks, gotta head to our exec sync soon, quick recap and next steps?
[07:48] Samir Patel: Recap: Redwood shows ~1.8x median improvement and ~1.7x throughput improvement vs BaselineAI on your 512/800 token sets after KV caching + quantization + batch tuning. Action items: we share full spreadsheet + logs, run focused 95th/99th percentile test, customer sends prompt set and network diagram.
[08:08] Maria Lopez: Great. Jared, Priya, will you own sending those?
[08:12] Jared Kim: Yup I'll send the prompt set and SLOs today.
[08:15] Priya Rao: I'll get the network diagram over by next week.
[08:18] Samir Patel: Perfect. Jules, anything to add?
[08:22] Jules Nguyen: I'll schedule the tail-latency 30m run and include p99 telemetry and CPU/gpu mem traces. Expect results by 2026-03-04.
[08:33] Ava Brooks: I'll drop the security packet and pricing breakdown after the call.
[08:38] Diego Martinez: Thanks everyone.
[08:40] Maria Lopez: Thanks - we're good.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription had minor speaker mislabels and a few garbled lines; product names sometimes transcribed (eg "KV cache" appeared as "K V cache").
